item.content:encoded:
Destroying the SCP Foundation with facts and logic

This SCP touched on a deep-rooted fear I have that I've never really been able to put into words. The outright idolization of logic and unyielding mathematical fact by so-called "intellectuals" has always unsettled me, and to see that taken to such an extreme in this article was incredibly disturbing. LordStonefish's articles (or at least articles that he's contributed to) always seem to be able to unearth these primal phobias that no other writer can really scratch, and it always leaves me suitably unsettled. Solid +1.

item.content:encoded: Having a background in theology, I was expecting most of this article to go straight over my head. This was a fascinating subversion of my expectations. I especially enjoyed the journal entries and interviews, with all their pseudo-religious rambling and symbolism. I can’t decide what the scariest thing about this anomaly is- the behaviour it causes, or the fact that there’s no obvious reason for becoming affected. Like, there’s no infection, people are just… becoming anomalous by thinking too much about a certain type of math? That’s terrifying to me. Upvoted.

No-vote. There isn't enough of a payoff, imo (e.g., we still don't have any idea why this is happening), and I think there's actually more detail here than is necessary. The many elements of the anomaly don't really cohere in a way that leaves a strong impression in my mind.

Also, although the description implies that SCP-3380-A instances have derision towards / would like to de-fund non-STEM subject matter, this isn't really exhibited in any of the interviews. They're mostly just really gung-ho about mathematics - which also makes it odd that the anomaly is mostly oriented around mathematics, but for some reason biology and computer engineering get involved as well.

item.content:encoded:
I'll just copy paste a relevant post I made on reddit about the meaning of this.

Just a disclaimer from one of the writers of this SCP. This SCP isn't meant to be an attack on atheism or STEM (I'm an atheist and I'll likely end up in a STEM career). This is about how atheism and a love for STEM can be taken to the extremes, in this case turning into a fanatic cult that thinks STEM is superior to all else and that anyone that isn't an atheist is lesser than them. That and an admittedly blatant parody of militant atheists and STEMlords.

With regards to stereotypes, this is only based on loose stereotypes regarding militant atheists and STEMlords, with the compulsions of the anomaly playing a much larger role. The MRA mention was a one-off thing and wasn't meant to be the main focus of the article.

I'm sorry that you found this offensive, but I hope you understand that that wasn't the point of the article.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There certainly a lot of "radical atheist" internet trolls, who have convinced certain segments of the public that they are the face of atheism. Fuck 'em.

Yet atheism is actually a bit diverse? It really isn't the KKK. I swear.

I don't really care whether this was trying to satirize atheists in general, or just the weirdo trolls. I downvote either way, because I'm bored of the stereotypes, e.g. that atheists treat Dawkins as a holy text, or that atheists are all men, or all Westerners. Also, the stereotype in STEM fields is that mathematicians are more religious than other scientists, so this article doesn't even get the stereotypes right. Also, about half of atheists grew up in a religious household, so the idea that they mostly don't understand, or hate, religious people? Not likely.

There was obviously some religious/political point being made here. If the point is that "atheists are sometimes awful people", that's both true and a point that doesn't need to be made, because it's already pretty well-known. If the point is that MRA's are bad, and also they are sometimes atheists, that's not actually what this article seems to be getting at, so it hasn't been executed well. It does seem to mention atheism slightly more than misogyny, which really messes up the priorities if it's supposed to be an anti-MRA piece.

However, if the point was "I think atheists suck and I want to write a thinly veiled complaint about them to justify my feelings", you are picking on a religious minority by constructing straw men to misrepresent them, which is morally wrong, and you should feel a deep sense of shame about your vindictive cruelty. Just my two cents.
